text: Kinyaz Scender Dragosti (also known as Scander) ruled Veil Sangora, having taken the throne in 1324 after his father died in a hunting accident; his son Catalin later fled when the Verkieri under Brenis seized power.
After nine years of oppression, the people of Veil Sangora rose against Kinyaz Scender Dragosti.
Kinyaz Scender Dragosti crushed the uprising at Shrikes Crag, massacring the peasants and leaving no survivors.
On a full moon night in 1347, a peasant named Cohen fled with his dying sister Luca from soldiers of Kinyaz Scender Dragosti who were ordered to kill anyone showing signs of plague infection.
Cohen and Luca were cornered by soldiers among the ruins of an old church.
Four vampires called Vrakieri, led by Brenis, ambushed and killed Kinyaz Scender Dragosti's soldiers at the church.
Cohen begged Brenis to save his dying sister Luca, and Brenis healed her plague symptoms by giving her some of his tainted blood.
The Vrakieri drained Kinyaz Scender Dragosti of all his blood as he begged for mercy, killing him.
That same night, Brenis and his three boyers, Ambress, Bakir, and Zanthy, seized control of Veil Sangora.
Brenis and his boyers slaughtered most of the local nobility, turning some into blood donors and others into court jesters.
Brenis abolished all taxes except the blood tithe owed to the Vrakieri rulers.
By 1349, two years after the Vrakieri takeover, the mining village of Lazla still had to pay the blood tithe.
Esme became too weak to attend the blood mass, putting her at risk of being deemed worthless and killed by the Vrakieri.
Cohen's father Pieta sent him to the village herbalist Anka for a tonic to help Esme.
While fishing with his siblings Jana, Lunka, and Meto, Cohen was confronted by one of Brenis's soldiers asking about Pieta.
An Uryashi commander intervened to stop the soldier from threatening Cohen's sister Jana.
After the Vrakieri takeover, Brenis invited the Uryashi into his service, and many left their mountain villages to serve him.
Cohen found his father Pieta arguing with neighbor Vladimir about time running out for a secret plan.
Vladimir asked Pieta to lead the men of Lazla to an abandoned silver mine to extract silver, which harms the Vrakieri.
Cohen discovered that Lazar had been killed inside a cave after fleeing a wolf attack, and someone had murdered him there deliberately.
Inside the cave, Cohen found an ancient tomb of a great warrior woman who fought the Vrakieri long ago and chose to burn herself rather than be turned into one.
Vladimir told Cohen the resistance planned to attack the silver mine while Brenis was away, with approval from resistance leader Craig.
Brenis singled out the weakened Esme at the blood mass, calling her a sickly sheep to be culled, prompting Cohen to publicly call him a monster.
Pieta decided to lead the miners in a defense of the silver mine after realizing Esme's death was otherwise inevitable.
Brenis's soldiers attacked the silver mine, having learned of the rebels' plan in advance.
During the mine battle, black mist and blood-red moths burst in and knocked Cohen unconscious.
Cohen, sensing blood from wounded miner Costl, lost control and bit him, feeding on his blood.
While feeding, Cohen recalled that Brenis had torn out one of his own fangs and pierced Cohen's heart with it, turning him into a Vrakieri.
Pieta had begged Brenis to spare Cohen's life, and Brenis granted the request by turning Cohen instead of killing him.
Costl attacked the newly turned Cohen with a dagger, causing both to fall into a mineshaft.
Cohen emerged from the caves to find his village Lazla burned and its people killed or taken by Brenis's forces.
Brenis forced Pieta to watch the destruction of Lazla, blaming him for the villagers' resistance to the blood tithe.
Brenis cut Pieta to tempt Cohen's bloodlust, but Cohen restrained himself and refused to kill his father.
Brenis defeated Cohen in battle and bit him, but Cohen's blood burned and weakened Brenis from within.
Brenis pinned Cohen to a tree with a pickaxe and left him to die at dawn, unable to understand why Cohen's blood harmed him.
Cohen survived being impaled and left in sunlight, later found alive by Anka who nursed him back to health.
Anka used necromantic magic to question a dead soldier, learning that the villagers of Lazla were taken to Brenis's castle dungeons for his coronation.
Brenis's coronation, where the captured villagers' blood would be used, was set to occur in 30 days.
Cohen learned that the miller Mert was a member of the resistance group called the Manommits.
Mert was captured and imprisoned at Stonewood Post after being suspected of belonging to the rebel cell.
Cohen infiltrated Stonewood Post, freed Mert, and fought his way out after learning of a resistance meeting point.
Cohen rescued the rebel Sarah from Brenis's soldiers near a bridge, and she led him toward the Manommit camp.
Sarah led Cohen into an ambush by the Manommits, who captured him using a silver chain.
Manommit leader Craig was skeptical of Cohen but agreed to consider an alliance if Cohen kept disrupting Brenis's forces.
Vulk and Pieta had been mercenaries together, fighting in Ireland, Constantinople, and for the King of France.
Pieta retired from mercenary life about 20 years earlier after the Battle of Cassell.
Vulk was captured and tortured five years before the story, losing his eyes, before eventually finding Pieta in Veil Sangora.
Cohen and Vulk searched unsuccessfully for gold Pieta supposedly received from the King of France after the Battle of Cassell.
A monk at Marrair Monastery revealed that Pieta had donated all his gold to build a scriptorium, seeking atonement for burning the city of Cassell and its people.
After Cohen's visits, soldiers attacked Vulk's shack looking for Cohen, but Vulk killed them rather than betray him.
Cohen raided Vrakieri boyer camps and caravans to disrupt their logistics and gain combat experience.

As a novice at St. Tina's Convent, Anka discovered a hidden forbidden library and shared the secret with her friend Leonica, whose reading of the books led her to bargain with a dark power to try to save the convent from the plague.
Leonica betrayed Anka by reporting her interest in magic to Mother Superior Bernice, resulting in Anka's expulsion from the convent.
Pilgrims at St. Tina's Convent tore apart the corpse of Saint Tina hoping her relics would cure the plague, but it failed.
Some nuns sacrificed themselves to hide fragments of Saint Tina's relics; those killed by pilgrims rather than plague did not rise as undead.
In the convent catacombs, Anka and Cohen found Leonica performing a blood ritual using occult symbols matching those on Anka's hands and Cohen's skin.
Leonica explained she had prayed for God to save the convent from plague, received no answer, then turned to forbidden manuscripts and made a bargain with an entity with burning eyes and tentacles.
Leonica's bargain resulted in the infected nuns being cursed to rot alive without dying, their souls trapped in decaying bodies.

When Leonica was one step away from ending the curse on the convent, Anka warned Cohen, who killed her during the ritual, only learning afterward that Leonica had been trying to break the curse and free the nuns' souls.

Feeling responsible for the tragedy, Anka performed the ritual alone in the catacombs to free the cursed nuns' souls while Cohen waited in the library listening to inhuman sounds from the crypt, and afterward the undead nuns vanished.
The book Sancti Mihi Histori Vera reveals that Saint Mihi, believed by the valley's people to have fought dragons, actually fought the Verkieri.
According to the manuscript, Saint Mihi was a pagan who struck down a Verkier with a magically strengthened sword that cut through evil.
Saint Mihi's body was believed lost, but the manuscript claims he was buried with his belongings somewhere in Svartra.
Albertus devoted his life to studying the history of Veil Sangora, but the Verkieri banished him and destroyed his life's work when they seized power.
After Cohen defeated him, Saint Mihi revealed that Tobias had betrayed and imprisoned him centuries earlier.
Tobias was a monk who believed Mihi was a pagan sorcerer and imprisoned him underground, fabricating the church legend of St. Mihi despite the good Mihi had done.
Cohen found cave drawings made by cobalts depicting Mihi as a monstrous warrior who slaughtered many cobalts before being defeated by a lone cobalt hero who shattered his sword.
In Maragir, villagers celebrated Ambress's execution of former nobility by crucifixion, and feared Cohen as the Verkier-hunting dawn walker.
Cohen and Julen found Vera dead at an old pagan shrine after she went alone to find something to protect Julen from the poison.
After killing Ambress, Cohen found a report revealing that a new female Verkier had appeared near the northeastern wall of Svartra.
Farcus explained that Bakir killed most of his family but spared him and his brother Ducen, whom Bakir sexually abused and crippled after Ducen refused his advances.
Farcus's journal later revealed the ring's ritual to heal Ducen failed, crumbling to ash, after which Farcus went mad and mutilated his brother trying to fix him.
At the crime scene, Cohen found a threatening note from Dr. Simeon demanding D'vorah and Eli repay a debt by week's end.
Dr. Simeon researched the plague and tried to synthesize medicine from Verkier blood properties, since Verkier blood cured disease including the Black Death.
Dr. Simeon had removed Vicho's fangs for research, though they eventually grew back.
It was actually the transformed Dr. Simeon, not Vicho, who killed D'vorah and Eli during his mutation.
Cohen later discovered that Vicho, having lost control of his hunger, slaughtered a farm family who had known his secret, after Simeon had falsely blamed Vicho beforehand.
Cohen found a manumit scout named Buen dying, who revealed the Verkieri were constructing an army of artificial winged creatures rather than recruiting soldiers.
Buen's dying message included the code word 'Teayotim,' which referred to the ruined Church of St. Teotim in the Midens.
A note found on a corpse revealed that an apprentice named Svetana, acting for her master Aurelius, hired mercenaries to retrieve an encoded tome from a tomb beneath St. Tobias's cemetery.
Years before the main story, Cohen and his brother Alen disobeyed their father Pieta's warning and went onto thinning river ice; Alen fell through and drowned before help could save him.
Aurelius's records showed that in his most recent batch, only 3 of 11 prisoners successfully became gargoyles.
In Augusti, Cohen found the skeletons of Hila's parents in a house marked with a plague cross.
Tonis explained that Hila ran into the forest 10 years earlier while their father was beating their mother, and she never returned.
A previous squad sent by Leonard into Zanthy's castle never returned.
The matriarch explained that Brenis had defeated Isbrand in battle, then forced the Uryashi to imprison him in chains within their caves under threat of destroying the village.
For two years, corrupted cobalts had been eating Isbrand alive piece by piece while his body continually regenerated, absorbing his corruption.

Within Isbrand's memories, Cohen and Lacra witnessed that Brenis was once a Roman legion commander whose army was defeated in battle, after which he and survivors fled into a place haunted by otherworldly shadows.
Isbrand confronted the sole-surviving Brenis and offered him a choice: kneel and become a Verkieri, or die; Brenis chose to become a Verkieri.
After his transformation, Brenis returned to his estate, and Isbrand made him kill the guards who refused entry and confront his wife Helvia.
Brenis's wife Helvia did not recognize him as her husband and burned herself alive rather than go with him, as Isbrand forced Brenis to watch, severing his ties to his former life.
In another memory, Isbrand ordered Brenis to tear out Lacra's teeth as punishment for Brenis violating the ancient Verkieri laws, since Lacra was his progeny.
In the ruins beneath Svatra, Cohen and Lacra witnessed the final battle where Isbrand warned Brenis that beings called the Augurs would come for him for violating Verkieri law.
Cohen recalled that the dying Mihi in the crypt beneath Zvatra Cathedral had told him to trust the Augurs because they would save him.
Three Boyars, Bakir, Ambress, and Zanthy, came to Brenis's aid, and together they managed to defeat Isbrand in the ruins beneath Svatra.
Brenis declared afterward that he had mastered the power seeping from the ruins beneath Svatra, which comes directly from Anahora.
Brenis's coronation ritual is set to culminate in the sacrifice of every prisoner in his castle dungeons, including Cohen's family.
Long ago, near the tower where Cohen and Lacra are staying, Saint Mihi fought an ancient Verkieri/Vraker named Kalas, who could thin the veil between reality and Anahora.
Cohen and Lakra share deeply personal memories in the marsh to attract the wisps and be guided to Kalas's lair.
After consuming the Mandre and preparing fully, Cohen receives an invitation from Brenis proposing negotiations.

In the Manummit route, the rebels launch a surprise attack on an outpost while Catalin's army attacks from the other side to break the blockade of Veil Sangora, and Cohen personally turns the wheel to open the gates.
Craig reports that Brenis is performing a ritual using prisoners inside the castle, but Catalin dismisses this as superstition.
Cohen, Craig, Catalin, and fighters storm the castle through a secret passage beneath the mountains, the same route Catalin used to escape two years earlier when the Verkieri seized power.
Cohen and Craig find the prison cells empty, with no sign of where the prisoners were taken.
Catalin sends a group of Manummits on a suicidal assault to seize the armory despite their being too few in number.
Cohen and Craig find the desecrated corpse of Kenaz Scander sitting on the throne.
Brenis attacks Catalin in the throne room, and Craig sacrifices himself to protect Catalin, resulting in Craig's death.
Brenis badly wounds Catalin and then leaves, telling Cohen that his family is already waiting for him.
After defeating Zanthy's blood guard, Cohen kills the wounded Catalin himself, refusing to let him rule Veil Sangora.
Cohen finds his family seated at a table in the castle's dining hall, shrouded in crimson mist, with his youngest sister Luca missing.
Brenis reveals his plan to break every bone in Cohen's body, nail him to a wall, and force him to watch his family drained one by one.
Defeated, Brenis cuts open his palm to release a cloud of bloody mist that drags both himself and Cohen into Anahora.
Before vanishing into Anahora's wastelands, Brenis refuses to reveal what happened to Luca and promises he will have the last laugh.
In the Lakra route, Cohen and Lakra descend into the ruins beneath Zvatra to interrupt Brenis's ritual.
Inside the ritual chamber, a huge red sphere of blood churns while prisoners float around it.
Lakra destroys the blood sphere, breaking the active blood conduit through which Brenis was drawing strength from Anahora.
In this route, the Manummits and Catalin's forces have not yet begun their operation, leaving Cohen and Lakra to infiltrate the castle alone.
In this route, Cohen's family is found fused into Anahora's growth spreading through the castle, in a worse state than in the Manummit route.
Brenis blames Lakra for causing reality and Anahora to collide, and offers to let Cohen take his family and leave without pursuit.
Cohen refuses Brenis's offer and attacks him alongside Lakra.
During the battle, Brenis seriously wounds Lakra, but she is healed by the power of the Mandre flower she and Cohen had consumed earlier.
In the negotiation route, after Cohen kills Brenis's three major vassals Ambress, Baker, and Zanthy and reaches maximum infamy, Brenis offers a parley at Shrikes Crag.

At the parley, Brenis brings Pater as proof that Cohen's family is alive and offers to return them and spare Lasa, including exemption from the blood tithe, in exchange for the location of the Manummit hideout.
Cohen can accept the bargain by marking the Manummit hideout entrance for Brenis, leading to its forces massacring the Manummits.
Brenis personally captures Craig during the raid on the Manummit hideout, drinking his blood and taking him away.
